items.question: LeadMind AI is a recent company. How can I be sure you'll deliver?
items.answer:
LeadMind AI is not a tech startup discovering actuarial science. We are senior actuaries with 15 years of experience who chose to create a structure dedicated to AI applied to our profession.

We voluntarily limit our number of simultaneous projects (maximum 2) to guarantee the quality of each delivery. And we systematically propose a measurable pilot of 6 to 8 weeks with contractual KPIs before any long-term commitment.

Concretely: our first SFCR agent prototype is operational. We can show it to you.

items.question: Why not use ChatGPT or a generic AI tool for our reporting?
items.answer:
You can try. Most of our clients did before contacting us.

The problem: a generic tool doesn't know the structure of an SFCR, doesn't understand ACPR requirements, and doesn't know that the SCR coverage ratio isn't calculated like a standard solvency ratio. It will produce plausible but inaccurate text — exactly the type of error the ACPR sanctions.

Our AI agent was specifically designed for Solvency 2 reporting, by a team that has itself written and supervised these reports for 15 years.

items.question: Why trust a startup rather than Milliman or WTW?
items.answer:
If you need a Prophet actuarial model or a standard S2 audit, Milliman or WTW are the right choice. That's not our field.

Our field is what they don't do yet: automating your SFCR with generative AI, training your actuaries to use LLMs in their daily work, deploying AI agents that understand Solvency 2 logic.

We occupy a space that major firms don't address today. The question isn't 'big firm or small firm.' It's: 'who has already built what I'm looking for?' Our MVP works. We can show it to you.

items.question: It's expensive for an independent consultant.
items.answer:
Our daily rate reflects a dual expertise you won't find elsewhere: senior actuarial science and operational generative AI.

For comparison: a Milliman consultant is billed at EUR 1,800 to 3,000 per day. A Sia Partners consultant, EUR 1,200 to 1,800. Our rate is in the lower range of specialized consulting — with the advantage that you work directly with the expert, no intermediary.

What's expensive isn't the daily rate — it's a project that doesn't deliver. We commit to measurable results. If a pilot doesn't demonstrate the expected ROI within 6-8 weeks, you only pay for work completed.

items.question: All expertise rests on a small team. How do you handle continuity?
items.answer:
This is a point we take very seriously.

First, every deliverable is documented and reproducible. The AI agents we build don't depend on one person — they operate autonomously once deployed.

Second, we have a team of developers trained in our methods, capable of handling maintenance and ongoing support. Plus a network of identified senior freelancers for additional capacity.

Third, the training we provide to your teams is designed to make them autonomous. The goal isn't to create dependency, but to transfer skills.

items.question: What is the concrete return on investment?
items.answer:
On regulatory reporting: our clients see a 70% reduction in production time. For a team of 3-4 people mobilized for 3 weeks on the SFCR, that's the equivalent of 30 to 40 person-days saved per campaign.

At an average internal cost of EUR 600-800 per person-day, that represents EUR 18,000 to 32,000 in savings per reporting campaign — excluding qualitative gains (fewer errors, better traceability, enhanced compliance).

ROI is typically achieved from the first reporting cycle.

items.question: Do your solutions comply with ACPR and AI Act requirements?
items.answer:
Yes, by design. Three mechanisms:

1. Traceability: every generated element is linked to its data source. The audit trail is complete and exportable.

2. Human validation: no report is produced without review and approval by a qualified actuary. AI is an assistance tool, not an autonomous decision system.

3. AI Act compliance: we anticipate the requirements of the European AI regulation, particularly regarding transparency, documentation, and human oversight.

items.question: What does a typical engagement look like?
items.answer:
1. Scoping (1-2 weeks): We analyze your data, formats, and constraints. We define the scope and success criteria together.

2. Build (4-8 weeks): We develop and configure the AI agent adapted to your context. Iterative testing with your team.

3. Deployment (1-2 weeks): Production rollout, user training, complete documentation.

4. Follow-up (3 months included): Post-delivery support, adjustments, guidance through the first reporting campaign with the tool.

Total duration: 6 to 12 weeks depending on scope. First results visible from week 4.

items.question: Do you offer remote training?
items.answer:
Yes. Our training programs are available in-person and remotely (videoconference). Hybrid format is also possible.

For remote training, we use real-time collaboration tools that enable hands-on exercises and breakout groups, just like in-person sessions.

The recommended format depends on group size and objectives. We discuss this together during the scoping phase.

items.question: Can we start with a small project to test?
items.answer:
That's exactly what we recommend. Our 'pilot' offering is designed for this:

- Scope: SFCR automation only (narrative + export)
- Duration: 4 to 6 weeks
- Budget: starting at EUR 30,000
- Commitment: if the pilot results don't convince you, you don't continue

Most of our clients start here before expanding to RSR, QRT, and other regulatory deliverables.

items.question: Do you only work in actuarial science?
items.answer:
No. Actuarial science and quantitative finance are our credibility foundation — that's where we have 15 years of field experience. But our AI approach applies to other insurance and finance roles.

Underwriting, claims management, regulatory compliance, technical steering, client relations: whenever a process is repetitive with a strong documentary or regulatory component, it's a candidate for AI automation.

We always start from the business, not the technology. If your use case falls outside strict actuarial or financial scope, contact us: we'll tell you honestly whether we can help, and how.

about.founder_intro:
Herman Njouonang spent 15 years in actuarial science and quantitative finance. At MACSF, he led the Life Actuarial & Modeling department. At Credit Agricole Assurances, he was an ALM expert at one of Europe's leading bancassurers. At Generali, a savings inventory actuary.

ISUP graduate, CFA Charterholder — a certification opening the world of asset management, banking, and portfolio management —, Executive MBA from Paris Dauphine-PSL, he now teaches artificial intelligence at Dauphine-PSL within the Master 1 Insurance Law program.

In 2023, he discovered the potential of generative AI applied to quantitative professions. Over 3 years, he built, tested, and deployed AI solutions in real-world contexts: Solvency 2 regulatory reporting, Market SCR calculation, ALM modeling, portfolio management, technical team training.

He founded LeadMind AI with a simple conviction: AI augments the intelligence of actuarial and financial professions — so that teams spend less time producing and more time deciding.
